summary: Run 5 of M1-S03 — a § 4 test-only repair after reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M1.md run 7 (S2-F-12), narrower than run 4's S2-F-11 repair: with the § 0b System.runAs fix landed, the @TestSetup seed insert in all three test classes still failed FLS, every time, on Case.AccountId — a field none of the three createCases(count, null, null) call sites in this step ever needed. TestDataFactory.createCases/createContacts/createOpportunities assigned the lookup Id unconditionally in the constructor, so a null argument still counted as a populated field once Apex's default user-mode DML (API 67.0+) checked FLS on the insert. artefacts/M1-S03/classes/TestDataFactory.cls was replaced with a verbatim copy of the corrected templates/apex/tests/TestDataFactory.cls (diff empty, verified this run), which assigns each lookup only when its argument is non-null. No other file in this step changed: all three test classes already call createCases with accountId=null and none references Case.AccountId, so the corrected factory leaves the field genuinely unset for every call site here — the intent Gotcha 14 describes, not a change any test needed to make. deploy-order.md gained § 0c recording the repair and S2-F-12. The three previously-declared checkers plus skills/apex/test-class-standards/scripts/check_test_class_standards.py --manifest-dir artefacts/M1-S03/classes were re-run verbatim: 0 findings across all four. check-outputs is ok on all 20 declared paths.
confidence_rationale: MEDIUM per GATES.md Gate D: Gate B resolved the one symbol this run touches (TestDataFactory's lookup-assignment idiom, copied verbatim from the corrected template; 0 unresolved) and Gate C check 3 (compile) did not run — build_mode is design-only, there is no target_org_alias, and there is no offline Apex compiler in the sf CLI. This is a narrower repair than run 4: one file changed, zero lines of test-class logic touched, and the fix is a byte-identical adoption of a template the library already corrected. What would raise this to HIGH is a green dry run with --test-level RunSpecifiedTests or RunLocalTests, which no agent in this loop may perform.

findings.title: S2-F-12 closed: TestDataFactory no longer volunteers a lookup field no caller asked for
findings.detail: artefacts/M1-S03/classes/TestDataFactory.cls is now a verbatim copy of templates/apex/tests/TestDataFactory.cls (diff empty). createContacts, createOpportunities and createCases each construct the record without the lookup field and set it only inside `if (accountId != null) { record.AccountId = accountId; }`, rather than assigning a possibly-null parameter directly in the constructor's field list. Every createCases call in this step's three test classes (IntegrationFailureResendTest.cls:57, Tier2EscalationServiceTest.cls:61, Tier2WebhookQueueableTest.cls:64) already passes null for accountId and none references Case.AccountId anywhere in this step — verified by grep before and after this run — so the fix required no change to any test class.

findings.title: M1-S04 ships the same TestDataFactory.cls and needed the same fix, but is out of scope for this M1-S03-only repair
findings.detail: deploy-order.md § 2 already records that M1-S04 ships a byte-identical TestDataFactory.cls under its own artefacts, and mock_deploy.py's copy_artefacts rebases both onto the same assembled path, so whichever step's copy lands last wins at assembly. This run replaced only artefacts/M1-S03/classes/TestDataFactory.cls, per the task's explicit scope ("leave every other file in the step untouched"). If M1-S04's own copy is not independently corrected, the two are no longer byte-identical, and mock_deploy.py's known behaviour of the later step overwriting the earlier one means the assembled tree's correctness depends on which of M1-S03/M1-S04 mock_deploy.py copies second — not a guarantee either step alone controls.
findings.recommendation: Run the same repair against M1-S04's TestDataFactory.cls (or re-derive it once M1-S03's is corrected) before the next mock-deploy run with --test-level enabled, so the assembled tree does not depend on step-copy order.

process_observations.observation: Gotcha 13 (S2-F-11) and Gotcha 14 (S2-F-12) are the same category of defect — a fix that is offline-correct and only fails once a real permissioned user actually executes user-mode DML — discovered two mock-deploy runs apart because RunSpecifiedTests only started running in run 6. Every offline checker declared on this step, plus check_test_class_standards.py, was green through runs 2–6; neither gap was visible to any check that does not execute Apex as a real user. This is the second consecutive finding of this shape on this step, which suggests the library's test-data factory pattern itself — not just this build's use of it — was carrying the defect until the template was corrected.

M1-S04 ships an independent, byte-identical (pre-fix) copy of the same TestDataFactory.cls that was never in this run's scope to correct (S5-F-02). A build with two Apex steps sharing an undeclared template dependency now has two copies that must be corrected in lockstep by hand, exactly the coordination cost deploy-order.md § 2 already named as the reason an Apex-foundations step should exist.

Whether the target org's Tier2_Webhook_Admin permission set would have needed create-FLS on Case.AccountId if a future test legitimately needed the lookup is untested — this repair removes the unwanted field from the DML request rather than granting FLS for it, which is correct for every call site that exists today but is not itself a statement about what the permission set would need to grant if that changed.

M1-S04's own TestDataFactory.cls copy still carries the S2-F-12 defect and was out of this run's scope; a fresh dry run with --test-level RunSpecifiedTests over M1-S01..M1-S04 will re-surface the same AccountId failure for any M1-S04 test class that seeds Cases the same way, unless M1-S04 is repaired first.
